commands.seed: for r in "Widget:3:1250" "Gasket:12:499" "Flange:1:19999"; do IFS=: read -r n q p <<< "$r"; curl -fsS -o /dev/null -X POST --data-urlencode "name=$n" --data-urlencode "qty=$q" --data-urlencode "price=$p" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-3000}/add"; done

env.name: PORT
env.why: The only variable this app reads. A search of src/ for process.env, config-file reads and settings modules returns exactly one hit: src/server.js:15, `var port = process.env.PORT || 3000`. That port is the whole of the app's own origin — there is no base URL setting, no callback URL, no CORS allowlist and no feature flag anywhere in src/. 3000 is set explicitly rather than left to the `|| 3000` default so that app_url, the runbook and the port the process actually binds cannot drift apart.

dropped.why: Linting is the static gate's job: `bsf gates static` runs the repo's own linter and compares each rule's per-file count against .factory/guardrails/baselines.json. Putting it in `build` or `test` would turn a baselined violation into a build failure and would count the same finding twice. With this round's guardrails applied, `npm run lint` reports 36 violations (no-var 32, eqeqeq 3, no-console 1) on untouched code, so a build that included it would fail every time. It is still runnable in the sandbox once `npm ci` has run; it is just not in the build path.

Replaced with `npm ci`, which installs exactly what the committed package-lock.json pins and fails loudly if the lock file and package.json disagree, so the sandbox cannot silently resolve a different dependency tree from one round to the next. `npm ci` is the command actually run and verified here; `npm install` was not.

Replaced with the equivalent `node src/server.js` — `start` runs that same file. The trial stops the app by signalling the process group, and running node directly means there is no npm wrapper process between the signal and the server. `npm start` stays in the runbook as the command a developer would type.

dropped.what: the `## Verify by hand` steps as a build or test command
dropped.why: They are a human checklist, not a command. Each one was run here (see capabilities.exercised) and the results written into the runbook's Verify section, which is where a verifier agent will look for them. None of them belongs in commands.build or commands.test: there is nothing to assert against, so a command wrapping them would pass in an empty directory too and would push the measured tier down to static.

dropped.what: every production and deployment concern — there are none to drop
dropped.why: Recorded because the search found nothing rather than because nothing was looked for. There is no Dockerfile, no compose file, no devcontainer, no Procfile, no deploy script, no release step and no app CI: all 35 files under .github/workflows/ belong to the factory itself. So no ENTRYPOINT, no deploy command and no release step was read into this manifest, because none exists.

not_exercised.why: The repo has no test framework, no test file and no `test` script, so commands.test is null — a fact about the repo, not a gap in the sandbox. Until tests exist the tests gate has nothing of the repo's own to run and total coverage stays at the 0% floor in .factory/guardrails/coverage.json. Diff coverage (diff_min_pct 80) still applies, so the first change to src/ has to bring both its tests and the runner that executes them; adding that runner is a package.json change `npm ci` picks up, but commands.test then needs an amendment.

not_exercised.what: Anything that has to survive a restart
not_exercised.why: The store is two module-level variables in src/db.js (`items` and `nextId`). Every restart empties the table and resets ids to 1, and nothing is written to disk — confirmed here, where ids ran 1..6 within one process and the seed's data vanished with it. A change about durability, a schema, a migration or a move to a real database cannot be verified here; it would need a database service added by an amendment episode.

One node process holding state in its own heap: no cluster mode, no worker pool, no lock, no transaction. Two requests interleaving inside db.add or db.remove cannot be reproduced, and nothing about state shared across processes can be checked. require-atomic-updates is installed as a guardrail precisely because this class of bug has no runtime check here.

not_exercised.what: HTTPS, a reverse proxy, a non-localhost origin, or any deployment concern
not_exercised.why: The app listens on plain HTTP and the sandbox reaches it at 127.0.0.1:3000. The repo has no Dockerfile, compose file, devcontainer or deploy configuration, so nothing here describes another origin. Secure cookie flags, `trust proxy`, CORS, HSTS and host-based routing have no environment in this sandbox to be checked against.

express is the single runtime dependency and src/ makes no outbound network call of any kind, so there is nothing to stub and no provider test mode to name. The stubs list is empty because none is needed, not because one was skipped. A change that adds an outbound call needs an amendment episode to add its stub before it can be verified.

not_exercised.what: Authentication, authorization and anything behind a sign-in
not_exercised.why: There is nothing behind a sign-in to reach: no users, no sessions, no cookies, no identity provider and no authorization check anywhere in src/. Every one of the six routes is public and anonymous, and all six were exercised. This is a statement that the feature does not exist, not that an identity provider was left unstubbed.

not_exercised.what: The `env -i` closed-environment form of the install
not_exercised.why: Running `npm ci` under `env -i` with only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, CI and PORT failed here with EAI_AGAIN on registry.npmjs.org, because stripping the environment also strips this runner's proxy configuration. The same `npm ci` with the environment intact succeeded. So what is verified is that the install needs nothing of a developer's own environment beyond reaching the registry; what is not verified is that it works with the proxy settings removed. registry.npmjs.org is listed under egress for that reason.
